subject.title: Stability, installer auth, runtime compatibility, and context-management improvements

question: What secure product boundary should OpenClaw use for local dashboard token persistence and Codex/OpenAI OAuth propagation while splitting this umbrella into focused owner-trackable work?
rationale: The requested behavior spans credential persistence, OAuth refresh-material handling, runtime/package update safety, and session-state recovery, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent security and product contract.

options.title: Split by security and runtime owner
options.body: Keep this issue open as coordination, route dashboard auth, Codex/OpenAI auth, installer/runtime, final-turn, and context-hygiene fixes to narrower issues or PRs with security review.

options.title: Promote one stabilization program
options.body: Treat the issue as a release-level reliability program and require a maintainer-owned design before individual fixes proceed.

options.title: Close after mapping to narrower trackers
options.body: Close only after every acceptance criterion is covered by an open or merged canonical item and the remaining umbrella no longer carries unique context.

recommendation.title: Split by security and runtime owner
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as coordination, route dashboard auth, Codex/OpenAI auth, installer/runtime, final-turn, and context-hygiene fixes to narrower issues or PRs with security review.

likelyOwner.reason: The current source and recent merged PR history most consistently connect this person to the auth, dashboard, and agent-runner surfaces that need the product/security decision.
